title: Vector stream + bulk import orchestrator: resilient batch API and async job framework
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Deliver a unified ingestion surface that supports both low-latency streaming and high-throughput bulk import for embeddings. Goals: (1) Add a fault-tolerant batch API that can accept large payloads and convert to async jobs; (2) Offer a streaming façade for client-side incremental uploads with commit semantics; (3) Provide idempotency and deduplication guarantees across retries; (4) Ensure autoscaling-friendly partitioning and backpressure to meet latency SLOs and cost targets.
acceptance_criteria: Batch API accepts NDJSON or multipart with up to 1M vectors per job and responds with job_id and estimated shards
Streaming endpoint supports ordered append streams and a final commit call; partial uploads survive restarts
Server-side async job runs with checkpointing and produces deterministic outputs for duplicate submissions with same idempotency key
Retries (client/network) are idempotent within a 48h window; dedupe memory bounded by TTL and sharded by customer
End-to-end 99th pct latency for single-vector streaming path < 300ms (excluding generation), batch load throughput > 200k vectors/min per cluster when autoscaled
Observability: per-job metrics in Console (ingest-rate, failures, retry_count, dedupe_hits), and a dashboard template for SRE/Customer Success
E2E test harness with synthetic workload that validates ordering, dedupe, and at-least-once delivery semantics under simulated node failures

progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting. Agreed on two-surface model (streaming append + batch-import). Captured requirements in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Vector+Import+Orchestrator
2026-03-05: API contract v0 drafted. Decided to support NDJSON, multipart (gzip) and a streaming websocket with upload-session semantics. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3321

2026-03-07: Prototype runner implemented. Basic checkpointing to S3 works but >1M vectors requires sharding to avoid single-host OOM. Measured 80k vectors/min on single m-series instance with current implementation.
2026-03-09: Design review feedback: add deterministic partitioning by customer + job-id to guarantee dedupe isolation. Also require idempotency key TTL of 48h. Action: update schema and redis layout.

2026-03-11: Implemented idempotency store using per-customer Redis hashes + compacted tombstone list. Added a bloom-filter tier for fast negative checks. Initial benchmarks show negligible overhead for writes.

2026-03-12: Integration test failed under Kafka partition rebalance — duplicates observed. Root cause: race between commit and checkpoint flush. Mitigation: introduce atomic commit procedure using compare-and-swap via Redis and durable S3 checkpoint fencing.
2026-03-13: Hotfix landed for commit fencing (GH PR #3387). Re-ran chaos tests, duplicates reduced to zero in 50/50 runs. Next: harden telemetry and edge-case partial-failure return payloads.
Notes: work is blocked briefly by platform capacity for a large-scale preprod run scheduled 2026-03-20. We've requested additional GPUs and storage quota.
decisions: Use two public endpoints: /v1/embeddings/batch-import (sync ack -> async job) and /v1/embeddings/streaming-append (session-based streaming with final commit)
Idempotency is enforced via client-supplied idempotency_key string; server dedup window = 48 hours per customer
Checkpointing model: incremental S3 manifests + per-shard Redis offsets for quick recovery
Partial-failure model: job-level status plus per-record error file (NDJSON) that clients can download
We will not attempt at-most-once semantics across cross-cluster migrations initially; guarantee is at-least-once with dedupe
Autoscaling will be signaled by per-shard queue depth metric and job backlog thresholds exposed to Dedicated/Private customers
